sources.title: JPL planetary satellite discovery circumstances
sources.evidence: Read the 115-row Jupiter table; reconciled every Roman number, name, provisional designation and discovery reference to the frozen input.
sources.scope: All 115 input Jupiter identities; this table establishes identities and discovery citations, not surface products.

sources.title: JPL planetary satellite mean elements
sources.evidence: Read and matched all 115 individual satellite codes and rows. Eight use JUP365; 89 use JUP347; four use JUP348; fourteen use JUP349. Epoch 2000-01-01.5 TDB.
sources.scope: Local Laplace elements for eight regular moons; mean ecliptic elements for 107 irregulars. The table is not an independently validated runtime fit.

sources.title: JPL satellite physical parameters
sources.evidence: Jupiter table includes the eight inner/Galilean moons and Himalia; mean radii and related measurements are not terrain models.
sources.scope: Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto, Amalthea, Himalia, Thebe, Adrastea, Metis.

sources.title: PDS Stooke small-body shape models
sources.evidence: Read actual target list: its only Jupiter entries are Amalthea and Thebe. Release provides sampled radius models with modeled unseen regions, not global measured high-resolution terrain.
sources.scope: Jupiter membership: J5 Amalthea and J14 Thebe; other catalog targets were excluded.

sources.title: PDS Thomas other shape models
sources.evidence: Read nine-target release scope; no Jupiter satellite is included. A published Thomas shape illustration or dimensions do not establish a downloadable numeric mesh.
sources.scope: Ida, Gaspra, Mathilde, Vesta, Phobos, Deimos, Hyperion, Janus, Epimetheus; exact Jupiter identities checked for nonmembership.

sources.title: Grav et al. 2015, WISE/NEOWISE observations of irregular satellites
sources.evidence: Read paper, Tables 1–3 and individual-object discussion. Eleven Jovian thermal detections yield model-dependent effective diameters and albedos. Kalyke/Praxidike required 3–4 sigma stacking. Megaclite, Taygete and Iocaste were nondetections; Themisto was contaminated by Jupiter light.
sources.scope: Detections: Himalia, Elara, Pasiphae, Sinope, Lysithea, Carme, Ananke, Leda, Callirrhoe, Kalyke, Praxidike. PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.07820 ; DOI: https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/809/1/3

sources.title: Graykowski and Jewitt 2018, colors and shapes of irregular satellites
sources.evidence: Read Table 2 and shape-analysis method. Twenty Jovian targets have disk-integrated optical photometry; the inferred average shape distribution is statistical, not twenty individual recovered meshes or measured poles.
sources.scope: Actual Jupiter measurement rows: Sinope, Lysithea, Carme, Leda, Themisto, Megaclite, Taygete, Chaldene, Harpalyke, Kalyke, Iocaste, Erinome, Isonoe, Praxidike, Autonoe, Thyone, Hermippe, Callirrhoe, Eukelade, Cyllene. DOI: https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aab49b

sources.title: Grav et al. 2003, photometric survey of irregular satellites
sources.evidence: Read Tables 1–2: thirteen Jupiter targets measured in BVRI where detected. The paper spells Megaclite as Magaclite; reconciled through Jupiter XIX and S/2000 J8. Himalia/Elara/Leda shown elsewhere in plots are literature comparisons, not this table’s new measurements.
sources.scope: Measured targets: Pasiphae, Sinope, Lysithea, Carme, Ananke, Callirrhoe, Themisto, Kalyke, Iocaste, Harpalyke, Praxidike, Megaclite, Taygete. PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/astro-ph/0301016 ; DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icarus.2003.07.005

sources.title: Sharkey et al. 2025, JWST spectra of eight Jovian irregular satellites, v2
sources.evidence: Read September 2025 v2 and Table 1. Program 4028 January 2024 observations cover 0.7–5.1 microns. Point-source/disk-integrated NIRSpec spectra constrain broad absorption features, not geographically mapped composition. Himalia used medium-resolution gratings; the others prism.
sources.scope: Exactly Themisto, Himalia, Lysithea, Elara, Ananke, Carme, Pasiphae, Sinope. Authors describe a custom extraction and calibration workflow; model interpretations retain uncertainties.

sources.title: MAST DOI for JWST program 4028 data
sources.evidence: Read the DOI landing page and its archive-query link, linked by the primary paper. Identified source observation archive; did not acquire FITS observations or independently reduce spectra.

sources.title: USGS SIM3168 geologic map of Io
sources.evidence: Indexed official publication metadata identifies the 1:15,000,000 global geology map, pamphlet, readme, metadata and GIS ZIP. Direct publication/API retrieval returned 403; exact ZIP URL and schema remain unresolved.
sources.scope: Io; Voyager/Galileo-era mapping on the 2006 1-km mosaic. GIS is listed as 281.1 MB compressed; no archive was downloaded. A geologic unit map is interpretation, not an elevation or current activity map.

sources.title: USGS SIM3237 Ganymede global geologic GIS
sources.evidence: Read indexed official metadata: 3046 mapped objects, planetocentric/east-positive 0–360 degrees, RAND November 1999 control, radius 2632345 m, 1:15,000,000 scale. Geologic accuracy is limited by kilometer-scale base-map errors.
sources.scope: Global Ganymede geology. Publication https://pubs.usgs.gov/sim/3237/ lists a 107.3-MB database, but direct publication/API retrieval returned 403; exact ZIP link not independently resolved.

sources.title: USGS SIM3237 database readme
sources.evidence: Read indexed official readme: ArcGIS geodatabase plus shapefiles and a simple-cylindrical GeoTIFF basemap. This is a concrete GIS release; binary contents were not downloaded.
sources.scope: Ganymede SIM3237; geometry conversion, frame/radius reconciliation and legend semantics remain preparatory work.

sources.title: USGS controlled Europa digital terrain models
sources.evidence: Read methods, coverage and product descriptions for five regional photogrammetric DTMs. Confidence and figure-of-merit products are supplied; measured posting is finer than effective terrain resolution. Reprocessing corrected spacecraft-pointing use.
sources.scope: Cilix, Pwyll, Rhadamanthys chaos/pits, Yelland ridged plains, Agenor. All are regional; none supports filling the rest of Europa with measured relief. Paper DOI https://doi.org/10.3390/rs13245097

sources.title: Europa DTM STAC item and asset manifest
sources.evidence: Read complete five-item JSON: product IDs, asset URLs, footprints and confidence/FOM links. Raster bytes were not downloaded. Footprint bounding boxes must not be treated as wholly valid data.
sources.scope: Five exact products listed in the Markdown companion with DTM, confidence, FOM and provenance assets.

sources.title: PDS registered Europa Galileo NIMS archive
sources.evidence: Read PDS collection and bundle records plus indexed USGS documentation. Reprojected spectra include local/regional/global observations; CUB radiance, CIOF reflectance and COC geometry products are described. USGS maps are registered to the 2010 Europa 500-m V2 mosaic; this is not automatically the newer 2021 control network.
sources.scope: Europa 0.7–5.2-micron NIMS. DOI https://doi.org/10.17189/4sz4-5024 . USGS access https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/europa-galileo-nims-hyperspectral-map-products-registered-archive returned 403 directly; individual cube/label retrieval unresolved.

sources.title: USGS/NASA Galileo color view of Callisto, PIA03456
sources.evidence: Read official description of the complete global-disk color observation. It is a spacecraft-view image, not a supplied longitude/latitude global raster; unseen terrain cannot inherit its colors.
sources.scope: Callisto; potential dated observation view or later partial color mapping after raw-frame, calibration and camera geometry reconciliation.

sources.title: NASA Juno SRU Thebe observation, PIA26751
sources.evidence: Read NASA May 5, 2026 release describing the May 1 observation at about 5000 km range and about 3 km/pixel. This is a real new observation but is not finer than the existing best Galileo 1.96 km/pixel source.
sources.scope: Thebe; released display observation. Calibrated SRU image label, pointing and surface registration were not qualified.

priorities: Europa regional measured terrain with quality masks; registered NIMS spectral observations after release/registration checks.
Io and Ganymede released global geology GIS, after resolving publication access and coordinate conventions.
Himalia plus seven missing moons with JWST spectra; sixteen further missing moons with measured broadband/thermal photometry.
Thebe 2026 Juno observation and Callisto color full-disk view as bounded observation work.

limitations: This is a completed bounded source-feasibility survey, not release qualification, exhaustive literature proof of absence, or approval of 115 scenes.
Every row was individually reconciled to catalog, orbital identifier and actual measured-target lists; orbit-context decisions do not claim physical data can never exist.
No large data archive, image raster, SPK or FITS set was downloaded. No scene code, PR, commit, worktree, build or browser test was created.
JPL raw spellings Magaclite and Philophrosyn are preserved against Megaclite/519 and Philophrosyne/558. Jupiter LXXIII S/2003 J2 resolves to 55501, not an assumed 573.
IAUC9222/9252 returned 401. Their four moons remain individually reconciled through JPL; original notices were not read.
USGS SIM3168/SIM3237 direct pages/API returned 403; indexed official metadata/readme identify the releases, but exact GIS ZIP URLs/schema were not independently inspected.
NEOWISE CSV/XML and PDS satellite-colors browse were inaccessible. Measurement membership was established from primary paper tables, never from unread archive contents.

Europa STAC manifests and exact asset URLs were read; numeric rasters and their per-pixel validity were not processed. Its NIMS bundle is Europa-specific despite broad PDS context-target tags; no Io/Callisto spectral coverage was inherited.
JWST MAST DOI establishes available observation provenance. No final reduced table was acquired or reduction repeated; spectra constrain interpretations rather than unique surface-material maps.
Existing nine packages were inspected at the merged commit; current dirty checkout files were not taken as that release, and its earlier qualification claims were not re-tested.
